name: Height-field Gaussian Primitive
definition: A curved local chart primitive that combines the thin support of a 2D surfel with bending capability via a Gaussian-basis height field. It stores spatially varying appearance (color and opacity) on the same local domain, allowing a small number of patches to represent both smooth geometry and detailed texture.
summary: The Height-field Gaussian Primitive is a curved local chart using Gaussian-basis height fields to provide explicit surface intersections and camera-linear depth, unlike volumetric Gaussian splatting.
